LESSON: LISTENING 14.1.1 PRONUNCIATION: CONSONANT SOUNDS AND INTONATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.1: Listening 14.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant Sounds and Intonation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening 14.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant Sounds and Intonation, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should people pronounce words correctly? 2. How can one learn to pronounce words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening 14.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant Sounds and Intonation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
149

● Digital literacy: A learner uses digital tools to record themselves and share dramatised dialogues.

● Self-efficacy: A learner document their successes when writing and dramatising the conversations.

Values:
● Peace: A learner discusses proper pronunciation and accommodate those who cannot pronounce well due to mother

tongue or other influences.

● Respect: A learner learns to ask and answer yes/no and which questions politely.

Link to other subjects:

● Kiswahili, French, German, Indigenous Languages, and Arabic require skills in pronunciation and questioning

● Physical Health Education, to which the theme of outdoor sports is related

Suggested Learning Resources

Print with appropriate font size and colour contrast/braille tongue twisters, audio/visual recording, audio recorders, digital

devices with assistive technology.
